summary: Cascade unpin triggered by frontend reconnect during weighted rollout causes inconsistent model selection
description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled weighted canary rollout for rw-3b-text-v2, some tenant traffic (BrightWrite) observed mixed model outputs. Investigation shows that a frontend reconnect event caused a cascade unpin/unbind of the tenant session which then allowed fallback routing to a canary variant despite a route-level pin.

Impact: Multiple production customers experienced inconsistent completions for the same prompt set. BrightWrite reported user-visible quality regressions in ~8% of requests from a single region during the rollout window. This is impacting their enterprise SLA and evaluation of our rollout safety guarantees.

Observed behaviour: tenant session was pinned to rw-3b-text-v2 (stable) at route-level. During a client reconnect (frontend websocket reconnect to edge), affinity token on the edge was regenerated but not propagated to the orchestrator commit path. The orchestrator interpreted the reconnect as a stale session and removed the pin record for the tenant cohort. Subsequent health-probe smoothing and autoscaler-backed capacity movement triggered fallback routing to the canary rw-3b-text-v2-canary for a subset of requests, producing mixed outputs.
impact: Customer-facing quality regression (~8% of requests for BrightWrite during the event window), elevated error-rate on content checks downstream, enterprise customer escalated to CS. Potential breach of internal rollout guarantees for pinned routes.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a route pin for rw-3b-text-v2 at tenant scope.
2) Start a weighted canary rollout with 10% traffic to rw-3b-text-v2-canary in us-east-1.
3) Generate steady request stream from a single tenant session.
4) Trigger an edge frontend reconnect (simulate network blip or websocket reconnect) while session has in-flight requests and a pin commit in progress.
5) Observe routing logs: some subsequent requests are routed to canary variant despite pin.

Note: reproduces intermittently and more reliably when autoscaler moves a pod or when a health-check smoothing window coincides with the reconnect.

comments: Sofia Chen (Support): Customer reported mixed outputs at 14:02 UTC. Provided request IDs and sample prompts. Marking P1 due to enterprise SLA impact.

Devon Patel (SRE): Initial hypothesis: edge->orchestrator token mismatch on reconnect unbinds pin record. Collecting orchestrator and edge traces. Asked edge team to pull debug logs for 14:00-14:10 UTC.
Maya R. (Edge): Confirmed edge emitted regenerate token on reconnect. Logged the affinity header mutation. Forwarded trace to orchestrator team with timeline. (slack: #support, thread ts: 16438).

Orchestrator Eng (Luca): Found commit path race: if pin_commit is pending when affinity token changes, the commit is marked abandoned instead of re-associating with new token. Submitting hotfix to treat pending commits as idempotent across token rotations.
CS (Sofia): Sent BrightWrite temporary mitigation steps and asked them to avoid reconnect-causing client changes during rollout. Customer acknowledged workaround but requested a permanent fix.
Devon Patel (SRE): Deployed canary fix to staging, ran load test with simulated reconnects; no unbind observed in staging. Preparing controlled roll to prod with feature flag guard.
investigation_notes: Edge behavior: frontend reconnect regenerates affinity_token for session; edge rewrites affinity header to new value before forwarding.
Orchestrator path: pin_commit flow keeps a mapping token->pin. If token mutation occurs during commit, current code abandons old commit and does not attach pin to new token, leaving tenant unpinned.
Healthprobe interaction: when pin is vacated, health-smoothing may see fewer warm nodes and route a subset to canary based on fallback policy, producing mixed responses.
Frequency: observed in 3 customers in the same window (BrightWrite primary) across us-east-1. Only reproducible when reconnect coincides with commit window + autoscaler movement.
Related artifacts: slack thread #support (ts:16438), orchestration trace bundle s3://redwood-diagnostics/2026-03-10/pin-fix-bundle.tar.gz, PR drafted at github link above.
resolution_notes: Root cause: race in orchestrator pin_commit path when affinity token rotates during an in-flight commit. Abandoned commits left tenant unpinned and allowed fallback routing to canary variants.

Immediate workaround provided to customer: 1) apply a temporary route-level override to set pin_mode=force for the affected tenant during the rollout window; 2) avoid client reconnects during in-flight rollout if possible. Customer applied override and reported reduction of mixed outputs to <0.1%.

Fix implemented: change pin_commit logic to follow token rotation semantics: when a pending commit sees a new token for the same session, re-associate the commit to the new token instead of abandoning. Added idempotency guard and extra logging. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/879)

Rollout plan: merged to main, staged canary in prod-toy region 2026-03-11 03:00 UTC behind feature flag, monitored for 24h, then progressive rollout across us-east-1 region on 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC. No incidents reported post-rollout.

Follow-ups: update canary rollout runbook to include 'pin_commit token-rotation' check, add unit/integration tests covering reconnect window, add monitoring alert for abandoned_pin_commits in orchestrator metrics.
Customer communication: BrightWrite notified of root cause and fix on 2026-03-12. CS offered a credits adjustment under enterprise SLA; finance to handle.
